title: Canonical bundle character of a complete flag variety
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and with every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group having finite central kernel an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ (a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup), with character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$ and integer coroot pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Here a split maximal torus is a maximal subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$. Write $p:B\to T$ for the projection with kernel the unipotent radical and put $Q=S/B$. For $\mu\in X$ put $\widetilde\mu=\mu\circ p$ and $M_\mu=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\mu}$ [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], the invertible sheaf associated to the quotient action $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\widetilde\mu(b)z)$. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$, the actual character supplied by [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. The scheme $Q$ is smooth of pure dimension $N=|\Phi^+|$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Define its canonical invertible sheaf by $\omega_Q=\bigwedge^N\Omega^1_{Q/F}$. The sheaf $\Omega^1_{Q/F}$ is obtained by gluing the modules of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{A/F}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] on affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Q$. For a locally free module $E$, $\bigwedge^n E$ is its alternating exterior power (the quotient of $E^{\otimes n}$ by the alternating multilinearity relations), with $\bigwedge^0 E=\mathcal O_Q$. There is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Q$-modules $$\omega_Q\simeq\mathcal L_{2\widetilde\rho}=M_{-2\rho}.$$ This includes $N=0$, where both sides are $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$, and holds in every characteristic.

source.place: Section 2.1, equation (8), printed pp.63--64, WANTED locally; online author copy read at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~mbrion/fbook.pdf. Their L(nu)=G times^B k_(-nu) is our M_nu, so omega=L(-2rho)=M_(-2rho). Milne iAG2017 22.51, printed p.480, invokes the resulting Kodaira argument.

proof.text: Use semisimple implies reductive and the right $B$-torsor $S\to Q$ in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Since $B$ is smooth, [lem-sfb-homogeneous-cotangent-associated-bundle] applies. With $\mathfrak s=\operatorname{Lie}(S)$, $\mathfrak b=\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ and $V=(\mathfrak s/\mathfrak b)^\vee$, it gives $\Omega^1_{Q/F}\simeq S\times^B V$ and identifies its top exterior power with the associated determinant representation. In particular these are actual sheaves of differentials, with the contragredient stabilizer action.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $\mathfrak s=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak s_\alpha$ and every root space has dimension one. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], choose a regular $\lambda$ with $B=P(\lambda)$; then $\mathfrak b=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\mathfrak s_\alpha$. The positive-system partition in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] leaves exactly the negative roots in the quotient. Choose one nonzero vector in each $\mathfrak s_{-\alpha}$, $\alpha\in\Phi^+$. Their images form a basis of $\mathfrak s/\mathfrak b$. Thus $\dim V=N$; the preceding step proves smoothness and pure dimension $N$, as asserted.

proof.text: Let $v_\alpha$ be that quotient basis and $\ell_\alpha$ its dual basis. For every $F$-algebra $A$ and $t\in T(A)$, the contragredient action gives $(t\ell_\alpha)(v_\beta)=\ell_\alpha(t^{-1}v_\beta)=\beta(t)\delta_{\alpha\beta}$. Consequently $\eta=\bigwedge_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\ell_\alpha$ spans $D=\bigwedge^N V$, and $t\eta=(\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha(t))\eta$. This product is the character $\sum\alpha=2\rho$, using the character $\rho$ of [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. The one-dimensional $B$-representation $D$ defines a group-scheme character $\chi_D:B\to\mathbf G_m$. Its restriction to the unipotent radical $U$ is trivial by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial], applied to $U$ and $\mathbf G_m$. Since $B=U\rtimes T$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $\chi_D=(2\rho)\circ p=2\widetilde\rho$ on every test algebra.

source.place: Section 18c, pp.389--390; Section 21a, p.425; Theorem 21.11, pp.428--430; 21.29--21.35, pp.433--435. Expanded determinant calculation for Brion--Kumar Section 2.1 equation (8), printed p.64.

proof.text: The top-wedge comparison of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-cotangent-associated-bundle] now identifies $\omega_Q$ with the sheaf of $S\times^B D$. Via $\eta$, its quotient action is $(g,z)b=(gb,(2\widetilde\rho)(b)^{-1}z)$, precisely $\mathcal L_{2\widetilde\rho}$ in [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections]. Since $\widetilde{-2\rho}=-2\widetilde\rho$, this is $M_{-2\rho}$. When $N=0$, there are no roots; [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] gives $S=T=B$, hence $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$. The empty wedge and empty product are $F$ and $1$, so both sheaves are $\mathcal O_Q$. All computations use torus characters on arbitrary test algebras; none identifies a character with its differential or requires a characteristic restriction.
